title: Grafting in Plants
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Graft avocado or mango seedlings (whip or cleft graft) with grafting tape; the teacher handles the grafting knife or works beside the learner. Care for the grafted plants for the term.

skills.key_step: The child describes grafting (joining a scion from a good plant to a strong rootstock so they grow as one), names the scion, rootstock and union, common grafts and crops, and that the scion keeps its fruit type.
steps: Scion: shoot from the good plant.

board.do: Draw a seedling with a different shoot taped on top.

misconceptions.ask: In a graft, which part gives the roots?
misconceptions.repair: Label a grafted seedling: root (rootstock) at the bottom, shoot (scion) on top.

misconceptions.ask: Can a mango scion be grafted onto an avocado rootstock?
misconceptions.repair: Explain the tissues must match to grow as one.

misconceptions.ask: How is a grafted mango different from one grown from seed?
misconceptions.repair: Compare seedling mangoes (mixed fruit) with grafted ones.
Show a healed union after the tape is off.

checks.question: What is the scion?
checks.answer: the shoot from the good plant joined on top

checks.question: Name a crop that is often grafted.

skills.key_step: The child says the steps: choose rootstock and scion of the same kind, make clean matching cuts with a sharp clean knife (adult), line up the cambium, wrap firmly with tape, cover the scion top, label.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parts of a graft.
floor.question: Which part gives the roots?

board.do: Draw a stem cut across showing a green ring under the bark.

misconceptions.ask: What must touch for a graft to take?
misconceptions.repair: Show the thin green ring under the bark in a cut stem.

misconceptions.ask: Why is a sharp, clean knife used for grafting?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a smooth cut and a torn cut on a stem.
Show a loose graft that slipped apart.

misconceptions.ask: What happens if a scion dries before grafting?
misconceptions.repair: Leave a cut scion in the sun for an hour.

checks.question: What must line up in a graft?
Why use a sharp clean knife?
checks.answer: smooth cuts join and no disease gets in

skills.key_step: The child says how a graft is cared for: water, light shade, protect the union, remove rootstock shoots below the union, remove the tape after 6 to 8 weeks, watch for the scion to sprout.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how a graft is made.
floor.question: What is used to wrap the graft?

board.do: Draw a graft with a shoot growing below the tape.
Ask what to do with that shoot.

misconceptions.ask: What is done with shoots growing below the graft union?
misconceptions.repair: Show a graft where rootstock shoots took over.

misconceptions.ask: When is the grafting tape removed?
misconceptions.repair: Show a stem strangled by tape left on.

misconceptions.ask: Where is a new graft kept?
misconceptions.repair: Compare grafts in shade and sun after a week.

checks.question: What is done with shoots below the union?
When is the tape removed?
checks.answer: after the union heals, about 6 to 8 weeks

skills.key_step: The child appraises grafting purposes: repair (bridge grafts over damage), aesthetics (several colours on one plant), improvement (good fruit on a hardy rootstock, early fruiting), rejuvenation (topworking old trees), and picks the purpose for a case.
steps: Choose the purpose that solves it.

board.do: Write "an old tree gives poor fruit".

misconceptions.ask: A young mango tree has its bark eaten by goats. What can grafting do?

listen_for: Cut it down and plant a seed
misconceptions.ask: How can an old avocado tree with poor fruit be rejuvenated?
misconceptions.repair: Show a topworked tree fruiting in two years.

misconceptions.ask: Can grafting be used for beauty?
misconceptions.repair: Show a rose with two colours.

misconceptions.ask: Why graft a good variety onto a hardy local rootstock?
misconceptions.repair: Compare fruit of the scion parent and the rootstock parent.

checks.question: Which purpose is a two-colour rose?
How can grafting repair a damaged trunk?
